steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes; cook until tender yet still firm, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl.
Mash potatoes until smooth. Stir in sour cream, cream cheese, butter, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Cover; refrigerate 8 hours, or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a medium-sized baking dish.
Transfer potato mixture to the prepared baking dish. Bake in the preheated oven about 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody:
I've made this recipe several times since my initial review two years ago. As I was printing off the recipe for this Christmas prep, I read some of the more recent comments, and decided to add what I've learned in the past couple years: there's a big difference between doing it the day before vs the same day. When made the day before, it's stiffer and the sour cream and garlic (if you add that, as I do) are twice as strong. Much too strong, in my opinion. And you will need to re-mash with milk and butter to fluff it up, which means you lose half the benefit of doing it ahead of time.

I HIGHLY recommend doing it only a few hours before (3 or 4 has been just right, for me) and then putting it in a slow cooker on low until dinner. The flavor is prefect and it's still fluffy.

These potatoes are Killer!! I made them the day before & you do not have to worry that they won’t be delish the next day. For Thanksgiving, I opted to not add any cheese to the casserole, though I certainly will for other meals.
I used 10 MED/LG Russet potatoes, 8 oz. cream cheese, whole milk, and easily 4T of Plugra butter. salt & pepper to taste. I added 6 cloves of peeled, fresh garlic cloves to the boiling potato water. Do not overlook these boiled potatoes as they will become elastic. 
I drained, mashed (potatoes & garlic), then added other ingredients, placed all in an 8x8 greased casserole dish (you can use 9x9 or 9x13 ): let cool COMPLETELY. I pricked several holes in the top, filled those w a little milk, dabbed on even more butter, covered & refrigerated. Thanksgiving morning I took them out, uncovered, & let come to room temperature. About 2 1/2 hours before dinner time, I put the potatoes into my crock pot on LOW. 3 hrs is the max or they will get brown at edges of pot. I did add a bit of warmed milk, more butter & salt while they were warming.
You will be HAPPY. These are delicious & it’s nice to be able to prepare these ahead & not need to tie up oven space.
Enjoy!

Easy dish! I made and put immediately in the removable part of the crock pot that was sprayed with cooking spray. The next day I took it out of the fridge and put it in the other part of the crock pot and turned it on low for 3 hrs. It worked perfect and kept my oven free for other items. I wish I owned a ricer to mash the potatoes (I think they would have been creamier) and I did add a little shredded cheese to the ingredients. Other than that, I made exactly as described. Everyone loved them!

I made this for Christmas dinner and it was a hit! I did make it the day before and then put it in slow cooker with 1/2 c whipping cream and a couple more Tbl of butter. I will definitely make this again and add the bacon bits! Thanks for recipe!

I first made this several years ago, and since then, I am EXPECTED to bring it to every family Thanksgiving and Christmas dinner. :)
I use 5 lbs of russets, and the whole 8 oz brick of cream cheese, since that's how it comes from the store. 

Make sure your boiled potatoes are DRY after draining the water, before mixing in the other ingredients, and that the cream cheese and butter are very soft. Those steps are KEY.

Fantastic! I used garlic salt instead of onion powder, made the night before. Next day I placed them in the mixer to fluff up & added a bit of heavy whipping cream during the mixing process. Potatoes went into the slow cooker on low with a stick of butter cut up and placed on top. A few hour later they were ready. Bon Appétit! Everyone raved how delicious they were!!

These were very rich and tasty, but had some small lumps. I cooked until still slightly firm but enough to break apart easily when forked thinking they would continue to cook some the next day & didn't want mushy or gluey potatoes. I refrigerated in a glass container overnight then transferred to a non-stick sprayed crockpot to heat for about 2.5 hours on low (then put on 'warm' while serving) to save room in the oven. Worked great & had lots of compliments!

I made these a couple nights ago and they turned out great! I followed others' suggestions and used Onion & Chive cream cheese instead of regular. I didn't leave them overnight- I just popped it straight into the oven after mixing and they were still great. Leftovers the next day were good too. I just put them in a microwavable dish and covered them with a damp paper towel for a couple of minutes. Thank you for this recipe!

BIG HIT! Great way to save time on the day of an event. I made these for Superbowl Sunday. Prepared them with garlic cloves boiled along with the potatoes. Also, I used the crock pot idea, worked GREAT!! I had to double this recipe with huge potatoes, I did not measure the sour cream and cream cheese precisely, but added as much as I felt I needed to make it the consistency I liked. I did end up adding about a stick of butter and some half and half to make them creamier. Got many, many compliments, will definitely make again!!

I adjusted this recipe to feed 1400 people with Rave Reviews! We bought the potatoes already mashed and cold. By starting with everything cold, we didn't have to worry about cooling that much down safely. I am planning to make this for both Thanksgiving and Christmas for my Family.
It as fabulous! followed other reviews suggestions used onion & chive cream cheese. Also made hours ahead and put in crock pot. Scrumptious!!
I have been making these for at least twenty years... they are perfect for holidays, including tomorrow's Easter.

Delicious! I made this the day of and substituted half of the sour cream for whole milk, used 1 tsp garlic powder along w/ the teaspoon of onion powder and boiled the potatoes in beef boullion. Usually I have to add extra spices because it's too bland but this way was PERFECT!
Love that it can be done day ahead and very tasty.

My seven year old kid loves this so naturally I'm rating it five stars. My cream cheese comes in eight ounce packs so I used eight ounces of cream cheese. I used 64 ounces of russet potatoes last time and it was good. I generally make them and bake them all at once - no refrigeration.
Excellent! I made as written but reheated in crockpot.
